# Hydra ETL

> Hydra ETL is an open-source (AGPL-3.0) declarative ETL engine for Python 3.9+. Pipelines are described in YAML manifests, validated before any data is read or written, and run from a CLI (`hdrctl`), a REST API or a visual editor (Hydra Studio), all installed with `pip install hydra-etl`.

Key facts:
- One job = one source, an ordered list of transformations, one destination (four YAML files).
- Connectors: CSV, JSON, Parquet, MySQL/MariaDB, PostgreSQL, MongoDB, Web API. Engines: pandas and DuckDB, optional Rust acceleration.
- Workflows: DAG of jobs with dependencies, parallel branches, retries, cron/webhook triggers and actions.
- Ships an MCP server so AI assistants can write pipelines that Hydra validates.

## Docs

- [Get started](https://hydraetl.com/get-started/): what Hydra is and your first job
- [Install](https://hydraetl.com/install/): `pip install hydra-etl`, extras and troubleshooting
- [Hydra DSL reference](https://hydraetl.com/dsl/reference/): the YAML manifest language
- [Guide](https://hydraetl.com/guide/): every source, destination, transformation and workflow element
- [CLI tutorials](https://hydraetl.com/cli/): create, validate and run jobs with `hdrctl`
- [Studio tutorials](https://hydraetl.com/studio/): build jobs visually
- [VS Code extension](https://hydraetl.com/vscode/): completion and validation for manifests
